chapter: New York, Henderson and Charlie Johnson
title: Auditioning at Fletcher Henderson's house and Leora's remark
summary: A Washington friend sent him to Henderson's rehearsal, where he sight-read new music, and Leora Henderson, Russell Smith's wife, told him he'd be a nice trumpeter someday.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x:
So I was -- as I say, I got into New York. I was walking Seventh Avenue. I ran into a guy, he say -- what are you doing? I'm here, well I'm looking for a job. Okay. I knew him. I met him in Washington, D. C. He said 'well, Fletcher Henderson is looking for a trumpet player.' I said, 'he is?' Yeah. I said, 'where does he live?' He give me the address. Says 'they're in there rehearsing now.'

So I went up to Fletcher's house, knocked on the door, you know. I said my name is Herman Autrey. I was sent here. I heard that you wanted a trumpet. You know? So he says, okay, set down. So I took my horn out and I sit down. He starts passing out the music. He picked up his baton and came down. Bang! And I hit it. I didn't stop until I got to the end. He looked at me, and the other guys turned around and looked at me. He pulled out some more music. He pulled out two or three more.

I did the same thing. He said, 'what's your name?'

I said Herman Autrey. Where you from? (Laughs.) I told him. he calls his wife, 'Babe!' Come here! I want you to meet someone! Nobody's ever played my music like that. Where you from? Who are you? I said well, I just come into town.
He say 'uh, you never played -- you ever played -- you couldn't have played before, I wrote it last night. You couldn't have played it.'
I said well thank you, sir. And she looked at me, and I --
Leora. I didn't know her. I never met her before. So she took a listen, and she said you'll be a nice trumpet player some day.

I said who is this big wench to go and tell me how good I'll be some day, and I just played the man's music. Who is she? You know, I didn't know who she was. But later on I found out, she was a trumpet player herself, and the wife of Smitty -- Russell Smith.

And then somebody told me the story. She -- Russell Smithwas down -- got sick playing his show on Broadway, and Leora went down there, climbed into the pit, and took over and played the show for him. That's how good she was. I said unnhh! Now you know, you learn, you know. Man, I didn't know. I was a pretty nice boy. I said (unintelligible) (Laughs.)
